title: Ground states of the Paley Ising model
statement: Let p be a prime with p = 1 (mod 4) and let chi be the Legendre symbol modulo p. The Paley Ising model on p spins s_0, ..., s_(p-1) in {+1, -1} has energy E_p(s) = sum over 0 <= i < j <= p-1 of chi(j - i) s_i s_j: the couplings are +1 (antiferromagnetic) on the edges of the Paley graph P_p and -1 (ferromagnetic) on its non-edges. Determine the ground-state energy E_p = min over s of E_p(s). The headline cell is p = 101: find a configuration with E_101(s) < -480. Every E_p(s) is divisible by 4, and E_p >= -p^(3/2)/2 because the coupling matrix has eigenvalues +sqrt(p), -sqrt(p) and 0.
submission: Text file: the 101 spins s_0, ..., s_100 as a string of + and - (whitespace and lines starting with # are ignored), or as 101 integers 1 and -1.
score: the energy E_101(s), an integer (smaller is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: a configuration of energy -480 found by simulated annealing with single-flip descent (tools/src/ising.c)

context: Deterministic spin models whose couplings are explicit arithmetic functions can be as glassy as random ones: Bernasconi's low-autocorrelation model and the sine model of Marinari, Parisi and Ritort (J_ij = sin(2 pi i j / p)), whose ground states for p = 3 mod 4 are built from Legendre symbols, are the standard examples [MPR 1994, hep-th/9405148 and cond-mat/9406074; Borsari, Graffi and Unguendoli, cond-mat/9511019]. The Paley model is the Fourier dual of that picture: its coupling matrix is the circulant Legendre (Paley conference) matrix, whose eigenvectors are the additive characters with eigenvalues chi(k) sqrt(p), so a ground state is a +-1 vector as close as possible to the span of the non-residue frequencies. It is also a signed maximum cut of K_p with the Paley signs, linking it to the pseudo-randomness of Paley graphs; the ratio E_p / (-p^(3/2)/2) measures how well +-1 vectors can follow that eigenspace (0.92 at p = 29, 0.95 at p = 101 for our best states).
references: E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ritort, Replica field theory for deterministic models: binary sequences with low autocorrelation, J. Phys. A 27 (1994) 7615, arXiv:hep-th/9405148
E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ritort, Replica field theory for deterministic models (II): a non-random spin glass with glassy behaviour, J. Phys. A 27 (1994) 7647, arXiv:cond-mat/9406074
I. Borsari, S. Graffi, F. Unguendoli, Ground states for a class of deterministic spin models with glassy behaviour, arXiv:cond-mat/9511019
J. Bernasconi, Low autocorrelation binary sequences: statistical mechanics and configuration space analysis, J. Physique 48 (1987) 559
R. E. A. C. Paley, On orthogonal matrices, J. Math. Phys. 12 (1933) 311

novelty.verdict: new. No paper, OEIS entry or keeper table found for the Ising model with Legendre-symbol (Paley) couplings or for its ground-state energies. The closest work is the sine model of Marinari, Parisi and Ritort, where Legendre symbols appear as ground states rather than as couplings.
closest: Marinari, Parisi and Ritort's sine model and Borsari, Graffi and Unguendoli (cond-mat/9511019): couplings sin(2 pi i j/p), Legendre-symbol ground states for p = 3 mod 4. Here the Legendre symbol is the coupling, the matrix is circulant, and the ground states are unknown.
novelty.benchmark: no Ising or max-cut family; the benchmark's Paley-related entries are Ramsey colourings, a different quantity

first_values.note: Exact values come from enumerating all 2^(p-1) configurations with s_0 = +1 (the energy is invariant under s -> -s). Best known values for p >= 37 are ours (simulated annealing, 30 restarts of 20,000 sweeps, then single-flip descent); they are upper bounds.

baseline.text: -480 for p = 101, held by Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: the configuration in `refs/paley-ising.txt`, found by simulated annealing (tools/src/ising.c, `ising anneal`). The exact values for p <= 29 come from `ising exact` (all configurations, Gray code). Lower bound for p = 101: -504 (spectral bound -p^(3/2)/2 = -507.5..., rounded up to a multiple of 4).

bound.source: E_p >= -p^(3/2)/2 (eigenvalues of the Paley conference matrix) and E_p = 0 mod 4
